doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Public-address microphones and the first Neumann in America
summary: He used PA microphones early, then got one of two Neumann microphones imported, the other going to Reeves Sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: And the microphones they used to use back in those days were?

Well in the early days they couldn’t afford the real expensive studio types so they had the P.A type microphones, they used in the public address microphones, so I had a bunch of those. As time went on I acquired a bunch of professional microphones and a mixer.
What was the…when did Neumann come into the picture for example?

Well that was, could have been later. The Neumann microphone, he was developing those of course in Europe, had refined it to a great degree, and they decided to sell it in this country. In this country they ordered two of them. One was for a film studio called Reeves Sound in New York, and the other was for me. Then I started using that in the home recordings that I was making.
